newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan denies helping plan Sri Lanka offensive.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan denies helping plan Sri Lanka offensive.

text.p: Pakistan denied on Friday a charge by Sri Lanka's Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels that Pakistani military officials had helped Sri Lankan troops plan the current month-long anti-LTTE offensive.
"There is no truth in this allegation," a Pakistan Foreign Ministry spokesman told reporters at a news briefing.
"We would be the last country to interfere in the internal affairs of a friendly country like Sri Lanka," he said.
An LTTE statement earlier said: "Sri Lanka's Operation Jaya Sikuru -- the military operation currently in progress -- was planned jointly with Pakistani military officials."
It said the rebels had received the information from reliable independent sources.
A spokesman for the Pakistani High Commission (embassy) in Colombo also denied that Islamabad was in any way involved in the conflict.

"We totally deny it. The conflict is an internal affair of Sri Lanka. Pakistan does not interfere in the internal matter of any country," the spokesman told Reuters. Officials at Sri Lanka's foreign ministry were not immediately available for comment.

Some 20,000 troops launched Operation Jaya Sikuru last month in an attempt to open a crucial highway linking the northern government-held town of Vavuniya to the Jaffna peninsula, 100 km (60 miles) further north.

The LTTE are fighting for a homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east. The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
